title: Character Encodings and Unicode
learning_outcomes: Explain what character encodings and unicode contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: ascii and utf-8.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Strings are sequences of bytes with encoding rules, not automatically user-perceived characters. Searching, transforming, matching, and displaying text require attention to Unicode and the output context. In this lesson, focus on ascii and utf-8; then compare it with bytes versus characters. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use character encodings and unicode when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Strings are sequences of bytes with encoding rules, not automatically user-perceived characters. Searching, transforming, matching, and displaying text require attention to Unicode and the output context. For character encodings and unicode, begin with ascii and utf-8. Also distinguish bytes versus characters; multibyte text; unicode normalization concepts. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
